summary: Deep parallel research on Hubspace/Afero cloud control for the Charleston 200-bulb canopy activation

research.headline: Afero's Hubspace cloud is fully mapped and controllable via the aioafero stack (api2.afero.net REST + Conclave TLS push gives you sub-2s state feedback), but there is NO sanctioned API program, the developer portal is dead, Afero is unreachable even to community maintainers, and no credible Matter support exists for Hubspace as of Sep 2026 — so the activation rides an unsanctioned-but-technically-solid cloud path with aggressive rate limits as the #1 bench risk.

findings.claim: Afero is the enterprise IoT PaaS behind Hubspace, and Hubspace is literally an Afero partner app — the Android package ID is io.afero.partner.hubspace
findings.detail: Afero (Los Altos, founded 2014 by Joe Britt and Shin Matsumura) runs a partner-tenant model: Home Depot's Hubspace and Kingfisher's Myko (Europe) are white-label deployments of the same platform. Home Depot Ventures is an investor, and the Jan 7 2026 CES 'Whole Home' announcement names Afero as the 'enterprise IoT platform and security backbone,' with TI chips and a Kwikset lock powered by Hubspace coming later in 2026. Platform claims: millions of devices, 200+ product categories, 50+ manufacturers.

findings.claim: The Hubspace cloud surface is: api2.afero.net (REST), semantics2.afero.net (data virtual-host), accounts.hubspaceconnect.com (Keycloak, realm 'thd'), with metadevice endpoints
findings.detail: From aioafero v1_const.py: API_HOST=api2.afero.net, API_DATA_HOST=semantics2.afero.net (sent as an HTTP Host header override on discovery/state GETs while the TLS connection goes to api2.afero.net), AUTH_OPENID_HOST=accounts.hubspaceconnect.com, AUTH_REALM=thd, client_id=hubspace_android, redirect=hubspace-app://loginredirect. Endpoints: GET /v1/users/me (account id), GET /v1/accounts/{id}/metadevices?expansions=state,capabilities,semantics (discovery), GET/PUT /v1/accounts/{id}/metadevices/{id}/state (state read/write as functionClass/functionInstance/value JSON), GET /v1/accounts/{id}/devices/{id}/versions (firmware).

findings.claim: Auth is Keycloak OAuth2 authorization-code + PKCE with HTML form scraping, ~2-minute access tokens, long-lived offline_access refresh tokens, and a possible OTP challenge that can break unattended kiosk logins
findings.detail: aioafero performs GET /auth/realms/thd/protocol/openid-connect/auth (PKCE challenge, scope 'openid offline_access'), scrapes the Keycloak login form (session_code/execution/tab_id), POSTs credentials to /login-actions/authenticate, then exchanges the code at /protocol/openid-connect/token; refresh uses scope 'openid email offline_access profile'. If Keycloak returns a kc-otp-login-form the library raises OTPRequired — fresh accounts logging in from a new IP may hit this, so pre-mint and persist refresh tokens before install week. Library defaults assume 118s access-token life; the Emkraan HA integration states 'Access tokens expire after 118 seconds' and refreshes proactively.

findings.claim: Conclave is Afero's realtime push service: a raw TLS socket (not WebSocket) with newline-delimited JSON frames, minted via POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/conclaveAccess — and aioafero 9.x fully implements it
findings.detail: The conclaveAccess response supplies host (e.g. conclave-stream1.afero.net), port, ssl, zlib compression flag, a short-lived SINGLE-USE socket token (not the OAuth JWT — using the JWT was the historic 'hello works, login rejected' bug) and channelId (the account UUID). Protocol: server hello/tunnel → client login frame {channelId, accessToken, type, version, protocol:2} → welcome; heartbeats are bare newline acks at a server-advertised interval (default 60s). Push events: private/attr_change (attribute id+value, mapped to functionClass via device semantics), private/status_change (available/visible/direct), public/invalidate kind=add|remove target=metadevices|devices for inventory changes. Mint a fresh token on every reconnect. This is how the kiosk bridge gets <2s confirmation that bulbs actually changed without hammering polls.

findings.claim: The historical developer Cloud API (api.afero.io) is documented and shows the partner-centric design: password-grant OAuth with per-partner Basic credentials, async attribute actions, and a full partner OTA pipeline
findings.detail: POST /oauth/token (HTTP Basic = base64(clientId:clientSecret), grant_type=password, token ~4h, example expires_in=16086, scope 'partner account'); GET /v1/users/me returns account + partner privileges; POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/devices/{deviceId}/actions submits attribute reads/writes with hex little-endian data and is explicitly ASYNCHRONOUS ('if the device is offline the request may never complete'); OTA endpoints live under /v1/ota/partners/{partnerId}/... (firmware types, pool, binaries, moveToRepository, deviceType associations, per-image push, tags). OAuth client credentials were 'issued to a partner and viewed in the Afero Profile Editor under VIEW > ACCOUNT INFO' with an explicit warning that developer credentials must not be used in production. Note this is the legacy developer surface — Hubspace consumer accounts live on api2.afero.net with the metadevice layer instead.

findings.claim: CRITICAL — there is NO sanctioned/commercial API access path usable for this activation: the developer portal is shut down, no partner program is publicly offered, and Afero does not answer integration inquiries
findings.detail: developer.afero.io 301-redirects to afero.io and all doc subpaths (CloudAPIs, Projects, Hardware, API-OAuthEndpoints etc.) return 404; the ReadTheDocs mirror (afero-docs.readthedocs.io) is partial and omits all Cloud API pages; console.afero.io is still live but only for existing partner accounts with no signup. The aioafero maintainer Christopher Dohmen wrote on Oct 3 2025: 'I have been unable to get in contact with Afero regarding a local integration' — no Afero or Home Depot response exists anywhere in the HA community thread. The only enterprise path is a business-development conversation (afero.io contact, 650-899-0091) or via the client's own Home Depot relationship — neither is a productized API nor achievable before Oct 20. Consequence: the kiosk bridge necessarily impersonates the Android app OAuth client (hubspace_android) on consumer accounts — technically stable (two active HA integrations do this at scale) but unsanctioned, so keep the client informed and hold Plan B (Art-Net/DMX) ready.

findings.claim: No credible Matter support exists for Hubspace as of Sep 19 2026 — Matter unlocks nothing for this activation and local control remains impossible on Hubspace bulbs
findings.detail: HowToGeek (Mar 2024) states Hubspace has no native HomeKit or Matter support; the CES 2025 product reveals and the Jan 7 2026 CES 'Whole Home' / Hubspace 2.0 announcements (Hubspace Connect switch-to-light binding, Circadian Lighting, Kwikset, TI) contain zero Matter mentions; CSA certification database keyword probes for 'hubspace' and 'afero' returned no entries; the only 'Matter-enabled Hubspace' claims come from SEO-farm review sites (smarthomiehub.com, roipad.com) with no sourcing. Hubspace 2.0's 'Hubspace Connect' is a proprietary device-to-device binding for switches/dimmers controlling lights off-circuit — not Matter, not an open local API, and not applicable to a Python bridge. Plan on cloud-only control for the ~200 A19 bulbs.

findings.claim: Afero rate-limits aggressively and publishes no quotas; community integrations floor per-device state polling at 2 seconds — write fan-out for 200 bulbs is the single biggest unquantified risk
findings.detail: The Emkraan HA integration README states 'Floored at 2s - Afero rate-limits aggressively' (default per-device delta poll 30s, discovery 3600s, stale-data grace 10min); jdeath/Hubspace-Homeassistant defaults to 900s REST polling with Conclave push default-on precisely to avoid REST pressure. aioafero hard-codes MAX_RETRIES=3 and pauses per-device polling after 3 consecutive 403s on state GETs (STATE_FETCH_FORBIDDEN_LIMIT), implying Afero serves 403s (not only 429s) under pressure. No public documentation of per-account/per-IP quotas exists anywhere — the Sep 23 bench gate must empirically find the 429/403 onset for burst PUTs to /metadevices/{id}/state. Official Afero attribute guidance ('no more than one write/update per second' per device) suggests server-side expectations are modest.

findings.claim: The Afero attribute model layers Hubspace 'metadevices' (semantic functionClass/functionInstance states) over raw numbered attributes, and writes are eventually-consistent by design
findings.detail: Core platform: devices expose typed attributes (MCU attributes numbered 1-1023; Boolean/SINT8/string types; one value per attribute), and official docs warn 'writing to ASR does not mean the attribute has been synchronized with the Cloud; synchronization may take some time.' The Hubspace layer translates raw attribute IDs to semantic states via per-device 'semantics' delivered in the discovery expansion — aioafero's conclave/semantics.py resolves Conclave attribute-id pushes back to functionClass/functionInstance (e.g. color-rgb, brightness, power). Practical effect: scene writes are async at two levels (REST accept ≠ device applied), so the Conclave attr_change stream is the only trustworthy 'bulb actually changed' signal for the acceptance metrics.

findings.claim: OTA is entirely partner-controlled (Home Depot/Afero can push firmware to the fleet), which is an event-week risk you can monitor but not block
findings.detail: The OTA pipeline (/v1/ota/partners/{partnerId}/... with per-deviceType firmware image associations and push) belongs to the partner realm — consumer accounts cannot schedule or veto updates. aioafero polls GET /v1/accounts/{id}/devices/{id}/versions every 6 hours to surface firmware versions. Mitigation for Oct 20-29: record all bulb firmware versions at install, re-check daily during the soak, and avoid tapping any update prompts in the Hubspace app; a mid-event fleet OTA wave would be visible as version changes plus temporary device unavailability.

findings.claim: The current library lineage is hubspace_async → aiohubspace (ended at 1.2.0) → aioafero, now at 9.3.0 released Sep 15 2026, actively maintained, MIT, Python >=3.12
findings.detail: aioafero (Chris Dohmen / Expl0dingBanana, MIT) is the canonical community client: typed controllers (light, lock, switch, fan, valve, thermostat, security system...) on AferoBridgeV1, Conclave push with REST fallback, split-device handling, and docs at aioafero.readthedocs.io. Two HA integrations consume it: jdeath/Hubspace-Homeassistant (381 stars, uses PyPI aioafero, Conclave default-on, 900s fallback poll) and Emkraan/homeassistant-hubspace (vendors a patched copy, 30s delta poll, per-device availability tracking, anti-cascade design). For the kiosk bridge, pin aioafero==9.3.0 and mirror Emkraan's proactive token refresh + per-device availability patterns.

findings.claim: No public Afero status page exists, so the activation needs its own health monitoring of the cloud dependency
findings.detail: status.afero.io does not resolve and afero.statuspage.io redirects to statuspage.io's homepage (no tenant). The Afero Console shows platform status to partners only. The bridge should therefore self-monitor: Conclave socket liveness (heartbeat interval ~60s), REST error rates, and a canary bulb per zone, with the <60s recovery target validated against deliberate WAN cuts rather than any vendor SLA.

bench_tests: Rate-limit onset mapping (gates everything): on one Hubspace account with 40 real bulbs, issue PUT /v1/accounts/{id}/metadevices/{id}/state bursts at concurrency 5/10/20/40, then sustain 100 scene changes; log first HTTP 429/403, any Retry-After headers, and whether limits are per-account, per-IP, or per-token by repeating from a second account on the same IP and the same account on a second IP.

Scene latency distribution: wire Apply→Conclave attr_change→camera-visible light change timing for a 40-bulb zone write; measure P50/P95 apply-start latency, first-to-last-bulb spread, and full-scene-correct time against the <2s/<5s/<10s targets, using the Conclave stream (not REST polls) as the applied-state oracle.

Server-side group fan-out probe: create a Hubspace app room/group containing 40 bulbs, discover whether the group appears as its own metadevice, and test whether one state PUT to the group metadevice changes all members (this would cut scene writes from 200 to 5 and likely dodge rate limits entirely).

Fresh-account login + OTP behavior: create the 5+ vignette accounts, log in via aioafero from the actual venue network hardware; record whether Keycloak serves kc-otp-login-form (OTPRequired), where the OTP is delivered, and confirm cached refresh tokens survive 8h+ soak and a 24h gap without interactive re-login.

Conclave resilience: verify conclaveAccess tokens are single-use on reconnect (mint fresh each time), run 5 concurrent Conclave sockets (one per account) from one IP for 8 hours checking for server-side disconnects, then cut WAN for 60s and 10min and measure reconnect + full state reconciliation time against the <60s recovery target.

OTA freeze check: record every bulb's firmware via GET /v1/accounts/{id}/devices/{id}/versions at bench start, monitor daily through the soak for unsolicited version changes or device-unavailable windows, and document bulb behavior (light output during update) if any OTA lands.
open_questions: What are the actual numeric rate limits (requests/min per account, per IP, per token) on api2.afero.net state writes, and does Afero throttle with 429+Retry-After or silent 403s? Nothing is published; only the bench can answer.

Do Hubspace room/group metadevices accept a single state PUT that fans out server-side to member bulbs? If yes, the 200-bulb canopy becomes 5 writes per scene and the rate-limit risk mostly evaporates; neither aioafero docs nor HA integrations confirm this.

Can the client's Home Depot relationship (this is a Home Depot-commissioned activation) unlock anything from Afero — even informal rate-limit whitelisting for 5 named accounts during Oct 20-29? Afero ignored the aioafero maintainer, but a THD-internal request is a different channel; needs a business-side ask this week given the Sep 23 gate.

Will Keycloak at accounts.hubspaceconnect.com challenge new venue-IP logins with OTP (and is it email OTP or TOTP), and are there account-lockout thresholds that 5 accounts × repeated bench logins could trip?

Is there any per-account device-count ceiling that ~200 bulbs on one canopy account would hit (Home Depot support anecdotes suggest large accounts degrade; separate accounts per vignette advice may exist partly for this)?

Has any single 2026 Hubspace SKU quietly shipped Matter (check retail packaging in-store and the CSA database manually via its JS search) — and specifically the 12A19060WRGBWH A19 color bulbs planned for the canopy?

research.headline: aioafero v9.3.0 (PyPI, Sep 15 2026; repo Expl0dingBanana/aioafero, Python >=3.12) gives typed async control of every device class the activation needs and just added opt-in Conclave TLS push, but it has NO Hubspace group/scene entities and NO client-side rate limiting — a Color Canopy scene change means ~200 individual PUTs (one per bulb) that our bridge must throttle and fan out itself.

findings.claim: Current package identity: aioafero (formerly aiohubspace, formerly hubspace-async) at github.com/Expl0dingBanana/aioafero, PyPI 'aioafero' v9.3.0 released Sep 15 2026, MIT, Python >=3.12, maintained by Christopher Dohmen (Expl0dingBanana).
findings.detail: PyPI shows 9.3.0 (Sep 15 2026), 9.2.1 (Sep 13), 9.2.0 (Sep 12), 9.1.0 (Sep 3), 9.0.1/9.0.0 (Aug 8-9), 8.0.0 (Aug 6), 7.0.x through Jan 1 2026 — roughly 17-21 releases in 2026 alone. Docs at aioafero.readthedocs.io. Older packages aiohubspace and hubspace-async are superseded; anything referencing aiohubspace is stale. Pin exact version for the install: 8.0.0 and 9.0.0 were breaking releases (8.0.0 reworked dual-channel lights + keyword-only set_state; 9.0.0 removed password auth from the bridge).

findings.claim: Auth is Keycloak OAuth2 + PKCE S256: host accounts.hubspaceconnect.com, realm 'thd', client_id 'hubspace_android', redirect_uri 'hubspace-app://loginredirect'; since v9.0.0 the bridge REQUIRES a refresh_token (no password login on the bridge), and initial login can hit an email-OTP challenge.
findings.detail: src/aioafero/v1/auth.py + v1_const.py: auth endpoint /protocol/openid-connect/auth (response_type=code, scope='openid offline_access', code_challenge_method=S256), credential POST to /login-actions/authenticate (form fields username/password/credentialId plus session_code/execution/tab_id scraped from the kc-form-login HTML via BeautifulSoup; header x-requested-with: io.afero.partner.hubspace), token POST to /protocol/openid-connect/token. Refresh POST sends grant_type=refresh_token, scope='openid email offline_access profile', client_id=hubspace_android. If login returns a kc-otp-login-form page, an OTPRequired exception is raised and you complete via submit_otp(code) which POSTs field 'emailCode'. TokenData persists to disk via to_session_dict()/from_session_dict(). Operational consequence for the 5 vignette accounts: perform initial logins and capture refresh tokens BEFORE install week (on-site logins from a new IP may trigger email OTP), then run kiosks from stored refresh tokens.

findings.claim: Token lifecycle: access token expiry taken from Keycloak's expires_in minus a 2s buffer, with a 118s fallback (DEFAULT_TOKEN_TIMEOUT=118, TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER=2); token() is guarded by a single asyncio.Lock so 200 concurrent requests won't stampede Keycloak, but they do all serialize briefly through that lock per request.
findings.detail: Verbatim from auth.py: `DEFAULT_TOKEN_TIMEOUT: Final[int] = 118`, `TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER: Final[int] = 2`, `async def token(...): async with self._async_lock:`. create_request() in v1/__init__.py awaits self._auth.token() on every API call and injects 'Authorization: Bearer {token}'. During an actual refresh (~hundreds of ms) all in-flight request creation blocks — a small, bounded latency spike that could land mid-scene-change; pre-warming the token right before Apply is a cheap mitigation in our bridge.

findings.claim: Complete REST surface (client 'hubspace'): auth on accounts.hubspaceconnect.com; account id from api2.afero.net GET /v1/users/me; everything device-related on semantics2.afero.net — GET /v1/accounts/{acct}/metadevices?expansions=state,capabilities,semantics (discovery), GET /v1/accounts/{acct}/metadevices/{id}/state (per-device state), PUT same path (set state), GET /v1/accounts/{acct}/devices/{id}/versions (firmware, every 6h); Conclave access via POST api2.afero.net /v1/accounts/{acct}/conclaveAccess.
findings.detail: v1_const.py verbatim: AFERO_CLIENTS['hubspace'] = {API_DATA_HOST: 'semantics2.afero.net', API_HOST: 'api2.afero.net', AUTH_DEFAULT_CLIENT_ID: 'hubspace_android', AUTH_DEFAULT_REDIRECT_URI: 'hubspace-app://loginredirect', AUTH_OPENID_HOST: 'accounts.hubspaceconnect.com', AUTH_REALM: 'thd'}. User-Agent template: 'Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 15; ${client_name} Build/test; wv) AppleWebKit/537.36' (client_name default 'aioafero'). Discovery adds units=fahrenheit param when configured. These are the exact hostnames to whitelist/QoS on the dedicated venue network.

findings.claim: Set-state wire format: PUT /v1/accounts/{acct}/metadevices/{metadevice_id}/state with JSON {'metadeviceId': id, 'values': [{'functionClass', 'functionInstance', 'value', 'lastUpdateTime'}...]}; one PUT per device only — the payload carries a single metadeviceId, so there is no multi-device batch write in this API as used by the library.
findings.detail: controllers/base.py update() flow: dataclass_to_afero() diffs desired features against cached state (skipping no-ops unless send_duplicate_states=True), features emit via iter_afero_values(), then a single PUT with content-type 'application/json; charset=utf-8'. Response 'values' are filtered back into the cache and emitted as RESOURCE_UPDATE_RESPONSE events, so the library's cache updates optimistically from the PUT response without waiting for the next poll. Multiple functionClasses for ONE bulb (power + brightness + color-rgb + color-mode) can ride in one PUT via LightController.set_state — use that, not sequential calls. For the canopy: a 5-zone scene = 40-200 PUTs; the kiosk bridge must implement its own concurrency window (the library provides none) and per-zone ordering.

findings.claim: RGB light payload specifics: power = functionClass 'power' (value 'on'/'off'; 'toggle' for per-channel), brightness = 'brightness' (int percent, functionInstance selects channel 'primary'/'color'/'white'/zone), RGB = 'color-rgb' with value {'color-rgb': {'r': 0-255, 'g': 0-255, 'b': 0-255}}, color temp = 'color-temperature' (numeric string, model-dependent optional suffix via a 'prefix' field — some bulbs expect e.g. '3000K'), mode = 'color-mode' ('color'/'white'/'sequence'/'night-light', dual-channel 'mixed'), effects = 'color-sequence' (functionInstance 'preset' plus a per-group instance).
findings.detail: From controllers/light.py + models/features.py verbatim api_value shapes. LightController methods: turn_on/turn_off, set_brightness, set_color_temperature, set_rgb(device_id, r, g, b), set_effect, set_white, and omnibus set_state(device_id, *, on, temperature, brightness, color_mode, color, effect, ...). Setting RGB requires color-mode='color' on many bulbs — set_state handles mode+color together; 'no-brightness' modes apply color-mode before power on turn-on. Multizone string lights arrive as split clones (one Light resource per zone) sharing a parent metadevice; split-device poll fix landed 9.2.1 (Sep 13 2026). ITEM_TYPES=[ResourceTypes.LIGHT] filtered from metadevices with typeId 'metadevice.device'.

findings.claim: NO first-class Hubspace GROUPS or SCENES: ResourceTypes has no scene/group member, discovery keeps only typeId=='metadevice.device' (rooms 'metadata.room' and homes 'metadata.home' exist in the enum but are filtered out of controllers), there is no scene/group controller or docs page, and the HA integration README doesn't surface scenes either.
findings.detail: models/resource.py enum: DEVICE='metadevice.device', HOME='metadata.home', ROOM='metadata.room', plus device classes light, power-outlet, door-lock, fan, switch, landscape-transformer, water-timer, thermostat, security-system(-keypad/-sensor), portable-air-conditioner, dehumidifier, exhaust-fan, unknown. event.py discovery filter verbatim: `if dev.get("typeId") == ResourceTypes.DEVICE.value and dev.get("description", {}).get("device", {}).get("deviceClass")`. Consequence: any scene the official Hubspace app stores server-side is invisible/untriggerable through aioafero — the kiosk must implement scenes client-side as per-bulb fan-out, OR we MITM the official app (the repo ships MITM capture docs at docs/ + 'Add MITM capture docs' commit Jul 25 2026) to find Afero's server-side scene-execution endpoint, which would collapse a 200-PUT scene change into one call if it exists.

findings.claim: Polling design: EventStream runs three asyncio loops — discovery (default 3600s), state polling (default 30s), and an event queue processor. Each state-poll cycle issues ONE GET per metadevice for ALL tracked devices concurrently via asyncio.gather with NO semaphore — with ~200 bulbs on one account that is a 200-request HTTPS burst every 30 seconds.
findings.detail: Verbatim from v1/__init__.py _fetch_all_device_states: builds active metadevice id set, `tasks = [self._fetch_device_states(mid) for mid in active_ids]; results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)`. Loop error backoff verbatim: `backoff_time = min(attempt * self.polling_interval, 600)` with DISCONNECTED/RECONNECTED events — so after an internet cut, first retry is ~30s (fits the <60s recovery target only if the first retry succeeds; second attempt waits 60s). Per-device 403 tracking: after STATE_FETCH_FORBIDDEN_LIMIT=3 consecutive Forbidden responses a device's state polls pause until the next successful discovery (feature added Aug 9 2026). For the canopy, consider polling_interval >= 60s or Conclave push to cut poll load, since Apply-confirmation can come from PUT responses instead.

findings.claim: Rate limiting/backoff is minimal and reactive only: request() retries at most MAX_RETRIES=3 with sleep 0.25s*attempt on HTTP 429/503/504, then raises ExceededMaximumRetries; 403 raises immediately; there is no proactive client-side throttle, no request semaphore, and no queueing — sustained 429s during a 200-PUT scene change would surface as failed bulbs.
findings.detail: Verbatim from v1/__init__.py request(): `while retries < v1_const.MAX_RETRIES: ... if retries > 1: retry_wait = 0.25 * retries; await asyncio.sleep(retry_wait); ... if resp.status in [429, 503, 504]: continue; if resp.status == 403: raise web_exceptions.HTTPForbidden`. Total worst-case retry budget is ~0.75s over 3 attempts — far too thin for a burst of 200 writes if Afero throttles per-account. Our bridge MUST wrap send_service_request/set_state in its own bounded-concurrency executor (e.g. semaphore of 10-25 in flight, per-zone waves) and treat ExceededMaximumRetries as a re-send trigger to meet 'zero wrong/missed bulbs across 100 scene changes'.

findings.claim: Real-time push exists but is 4 days old: v9.3.0 (Sep 15 2026) added an opt-in Conclave client (enable_conclave=True) — raw TCP+TLS (NOT websocket) to a host/port obtained from POST /v1/accounts/{acct}/conclaveAccess, JSON frames, server-driven heartbeats, 1s→60s doubling reconnect backoff, and REST true-up on reconnect.
findings.detail: conclave/access.py: POST body {'user': bool, 'softHub': bool}; response parsed for conclave.host/port/ssl(default True)/compression(default True) plus a 'short-lived single-use Conclave socket access token' (tokens[].token, channelId=account UUID, expiresTimestamp), preferring token type 'account'. conclave/client.py: asyncio.open_connection with SSL context + server_hostname, opening handshake '{}' then login frame; DEFAULT_READ_TIMEOUT=75.0s, WIRE_IDLE_HEARTBEAT_MULTIPLIER=2.0, heartbeat interval taken from server handshake, acks are bare newline; private frames = device state updates (handled serially under a lock), public frames = inventory add/delete; on reconnect it calls fetch_all_device_states() and regenerates events. Bridge starts Conclave only after the first REST discovery poll. The jdeath HA integration now treats REST polling as a 15-minute true-up when push is active. For the kiosk, push gives fast external-change awareness, but its maturity at 200 devices is unproven — do not make the show depend on it before the bench gate.

findings.claim: All four vignette device classes are supported with exact function classes: locks via 'lock-control' (LOCKING/UNLOCKING enum; LockController.lock/unlock), smart plugs/outlets via SwitchController ('power'/'toggle', functionInstance keys for multi-outlet; matches ResourceTypes SWITCH, POWER_OUTLET, LANDSCAPE_TRANSFORMER), ceiling fans via FanController ('power', 'fan-speed' percentage mapped to the model's ordered speed list, 'fan-reverse', 'comfort-breeze' preset toggle), and string lights as LIGHT-class devices (multizone ones appear as split per-zone Light resources).
findings.detail: AferoBridgeV1 instantiates 13 controllers: dehumidifiers, devices, exhaust_fans, fans, lights, locks, portable_acs, security_systems (+keypads +sensors), switches, thermostats, valves (water-timer). Humidifier for vignette 3: dehumidifier controller landed Sep 12 2026 (contributed PR); a plain humidifier likely rides the same platform — verify the actual SKU's deviceClass at bench. Defiant locks: only lock/unlock control, no code management. Fountain on outdoor smart plug = SwitchController.turn_on(device_id, instance=...).

bench_tests: Burst-write ceiling: from one account, fire concurrent PUT /v1/accounts/{acct}/metadevices/{id}/state to 40 real bulbs (one zone), then 200, at concurrency windows of 10/25/50/unbounded; record HTTP 429/503 counts, completion time, and whether aioafero's 3x0.25s retry ladder absorbs them — this directly determines the semaphore size our bridge needs and whether 5 separate accounts (one per zone) raise the ceiling.

Latency distribution: instrument Apply -> PUT sent -> bulb visibly changes for each of 200 bulbs across 100 scene changes; verify 95% <2s start, first-to-last spread <2s, full scene <5s; compare one combined PUT per bulb (power+brightness+color-rgb+color-mode in a single values[] array) vs sequential single-value PUTs.

Poll-load interaction: run the default 30s EventStream polling on the 200-bulb account WHILE executing scene changes; check whether the 200-GET poll burst steals bandwidth/attracts throttling that delays writes; retest with polling_interval=120s and with polling disabled (PUT-response-driven cache only).

Auth resilience: provision all 5 vignette accounts' refresh tokens off-site first; then on the venue network do a cold login to confirm whether Keycloak (accounts.hubspaceconnect.com, realm thd) triggers the email-OTP path (kc-otp-login-form) from a fresh IP; also measure token refresh time and verify no scene-change stalls when the asyncio.Lock'd refresh fires mid-burst (force by setting token_expiration in the past).

Wire-format edge cases on the actual EcoSmart A19 SKU: confirm color-temperature value format (plain '3000' vs suffixed '3000K') from the discovery capability definitions; confirm color-mode must be set to 'color' for color-rgb to take effect from white mode; measure whether identical repeated states are dropped by dataclass_to_afero (need send_duplicate_states=True for our idempotent re-send strategy).

MITM the official Hubspace Android app (repo's docs include MITM capture instructions) while creating/applying a 40-bulb group scene: capture whether Afero exposes a server-side group/scene-execution endpoint that applies one command to many devices — if it exists, one call could replace 200 PUTs and trivially beat the 2s spread target.

research.headline: The Home Assistant/aioafero ecosystem proves Hubspace cloud control is per-device-command only (no group/scene primitives, no transitions), throttled per account with 429/503 retries and a hardcoded 3-connection HTTP cap, so a stock Python bridge cannot hit a <2s first-to-last spread on 200 bulbs without patching concurrency, splitting accounts, and/or offloading animation to on-bulb sequence effects — while the days-old (Sep 15, 2026) Conclave push channel finally gives near-real-time state feedback.

findings.claim: The canonical community integration is jdeath/Hubspace-Homeassistant v8.3.0 (Sep 15, 2026) built on Expl0dingBanana/aioafero 9.3.0 (PyPI, Sep 15, 2026); the library was renamed from aiohubspace to aioafero at aioafero 2.0.0 (Apr 29, 2025) and previously superseded hubspace-async — report current names aioafero/Hubspace-Homeassistant, not aiohubspace.
findings.detail: Integration manifest pins aioafero==9.3.0, iot_class cloud_polling, requires Python >=3.12 for the lib; repo has 381 stars, 65 forks, created Mar 2022, pushed Sep 15 2026, 0 open issues (actively triaged). Release cadence is intense: 8.0.0 Aug 9, 8.1.0 Sep 13, 8.2.0 Sep 14, 8.3.0 Sep 15, 2026 — expect churn during the install window; pin versions for the show.

findings.claim: Supported device types cover every vignette need except true humidifiers: RGB/CCT lights (incl. LED string/strip lights with 'sequence' preset effects), plugs/outlets, switches, ceiling/exhaust fans, Defiant locks (lock/unlock/battery), water-timer valves, thermostats, portable ACs, dehumidifiers, security systems.
findings.detail: aioafero ships typed controllers: light, switch, fan, exhaust_fan, lock, valve, thermostat, portable_ac, dehumidifier, security_system(+keypad/sensor), device. Lights expose color-mode values color/white/sequence/mixed; dual-channel RGB+WW fixtures split into two HA entities (v7.0.0+). Dehumidifier support landed v8.1.0 via HA humidifier platform — a plain humidifier device class is NOT listed, so bench-verify the bedroom humidifier SKU early. String-light gaps documented: preset sequence speed not controllable (issue #205), white-mode quirks on strips (issue #148).

findings.claim: Hubspace app-defined groups, rooms, and scenes are NOT exposed: aioafero has no scene/group/room model or controller, and every write is a per-device REST PUT — so any 40-bulb zone change is 40 separate cloud calls, and the popcorn effect is structural, not a tuning problem.
findings.detail: aioafero source tree and device.py contain no scene/group/room classes; commands go through send_service_request(device_id, states) -> PUT per metadevice. Issue #204 ('Rooms not importing', closed Dec 2025) confirms room import was attempted and doesn't work. HA's own scene engine also fires per-light service calls sequentially. Nothing in the ecosystem batches multiple devices into one API call; if the raw Afero API has a group-command endpoint, no community code uses it (worth checking in the API research track).

findings.claim: aioafero hardcodes throughput ceilings that will strangle a 200-bulb scene apply: aiohttp TCP connector limited to 3 connections per host, MAX_RETRIES=3 with tiny linear backoff (0.25s*n) on 429/503/504, immediate hard-fail on 403, and per-device state-poll pausing after 3 consecutive 403s.
findings.detail: From v1/__init__.py and v1_const.py: retried statuses are exactly 429/503/504 (ExceededMaximumRetries after 3), backoff 0.25/0.5/0.75s; 403 raises HTTPForbidden instantly; STATE_FETCH_FORBIDDEN_LIMIT=3 pauses per-device polls (added 9.0.1 Aug 9, 2026 — meaning real users hit repeated 403s on state GETs). With 3 parallel connections, 200 sequential-ish PUTs at ~150-300ms each ≈ 10-20s to issue a full-canopy scene — far outside the <2s spread target. A custom bridge must raise the connector limit and empirically find the 429 onset; the 429-retry code proves Afero does send 429s.

findings.claim: Official troubleshooting docs confirm a per-ACCOUNT rate-limit quota shared by all clients: 'concurrent clients (phone app, Home Assistant, scripts) compete for the same quota' — which validates Home Depot's separate-account-per-vignette advice and suggests splitting the 200-bulb canopy across accounts multiplies write budget.
findings.detail: aioafero troubleshooting guide attributes 429s and stale/slow data to multiple clients on one account and prescribes longer polling_interval or fewer simultaneous integrations. No numeric req/min limit is published anywhere in the ecosystem. Multi-account is natively supported in the HA integration: config entries are keyed unique_id=username.lower() with no single_instance restriction, so 5+ accounts run side-by-side; whether Afero also throttles per source IP (all kiosk traffic NATed) is unknown and must be bench-tested.

findings.claim: Polling architecture and defaults: current v8.3.0 uses Conclave push by default with REST true-up polling at 900s (15 min) for new installs; pre-8.3 default was 30s account polling; HA options floor polling at 2s ('polling_too_short' error); aioafero library defaults are 30s state / 3600s discovery / 21600s firmware-version polls.
findings.detail: Poll cost scales linearly with device count: state fetches are per-device GETs to /v1/accounts/{acct}/metadevices/{id}/state gathered through the 3-connection cap. Real-world cost datapoint: 14 lights polled at 5s consumed ~1.5 GB/day (issue #216, Dec 30 2025), ~6KB per device state response; 200 bulbs at 5s would be ~50 req/s attempted and tens of GB/day — do not plan tight polling; use Conclave for state and poll rarely. Emkraan's rival integration uses 30s delta polls floored at 2s 'because Afero rate-limits aggressively'; matterbridge-hubspace uses 30s (min 5s).

findings.claim: Conclave — Afero's push channel — was reverse-engineered and shipped opt-in in aioafero 9.3.0 / enabled-by-default in HA 8.3.0 on Sep 15, 2026: TLS socket to conclave-stream1.afero.net:443, newline-delimited JSON with zlib compression, ~60s server heartbeats, subscribe-ONLY (all writes remain REST).
findings.detail: Access requires a short-lived token from POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/conclaveAccess (distinct from the OAuth bearer), login must complete <60s, stall detection after ~2 missed heartbeats (~120s), auto-reconnect with exponential backoff, pushes attr_change/status_change plus device add/remove envelopes into the same cache REST fills. For the kiosk this is the state-verification rail (detect wrong/missed bulbs in near real time without poll storms) — but it is 4 days old at research time (protocol 'conclave 2.7.3' per issue #228), so an 8h soak must validate its stability before relying on it for show ops.

findings.claim: Auth is Keycloak OAuth at accounts.hubspaceconnect.com (realm 'thd', client_id 'hubspace_android', redirect hubspace-app://loginredirect) with very short-lived access tokens (~118s per Emkraan; changelog: expires_in minus 2s buffer); since aioafero 9.0.0/HA v8.0.0 (Aug 8-9, 2026) passwords are no longer stored — sessions live on the refresh token, with OTP/MFA supported at login.
findings.detail: Breaking change caused a login-regression cluster (issue #256 Aug 18, 2026). The ~2-minute access-token life means any bridge must refresh constantly and proactively; Emkraan patches upstream aioafero with a 20s TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN because refresh-token failures caused infinite retry loops with no fallback to full login. For a 5-day retail activation: persist refresh tokens per account, implement full re-login fallback, and rehearse token revocation/password-change scenarios.

findings.claim: Scale evidence: the largest publicly documented deployment is 143 devices, and it suffered intermittent HA bootstrap failures ('Bootstrap stage 2 timeout' inside aioafero wait_for_first_poll, Jan 2026) that were never root-caused — nobody in the community visibly runs ~200 Hubspace devices on one account, so the canopy operates beyond all documented field experience.
findings.detail: Issue #222 (143 devices, HA 2026.1.2) resolved only empirically after upgrading to HA 2026.2.2; forum deployments are mostly 1-7 devices (fans, a dimmer, a dehumidifier); Hubitat port tester ran 7 fans. Historical latency complaint: 120s state-read delays with the 2023-era integration (issue #34, obsolete architecture). Positive datapoint: a single Home Depot dimmer ran a year with zero attention (HA forum, Mar 2026). The 200-bulb single-account configuration is unprecedented and must be treated as original research at the Sep 23 bench gate.

findings.claim: Cloud reliability incidents are documented but short: a ~43-minute window of HTTP 500 Internal Server Error + connection timeouts on api2.afero.net per-device state endpoints on Jul 27, 2026 (issue #240); upstream aioafero did NOT retry 500/502 or connection errors (only 429/503/504) until Emkraan patched it — a stock bridge freezes on stale data during such windows.
findings.detail: Emkraan's NOTICE.md also documents that aioafero's ~30s state-poll loop swallowed exceptions without emitting DISCONNECTED events, 'leaving devices frozen on stale data indefinitely' — directly relevant to the kiosk's <60s recovery target: the bridge must add its own disconnect detection and 500/502/timeout retry. Platform-churn warning: the Myko brand (also Afero-based) was force-migrated to Tuya-based Myko+ in Jan 2026, instantly breaking all community integration access for those users (issue #223) — precedent that Afero-platform access can vanish with a vendor decision; maintainer Expl0dingBanana said (Oct 2025) Afero never responded to requests for sanctioned local control.

findings.claim: No transition/fade support exists anywhere in the stack — the light controller docs document no fade or transition-time parameter — so canopy 'mood' scenes must be designed as hard cuts, slow cloud-stepped drifts (API-call-expensive and rate-limit-risky), or offloaded to on-bulb 'sequence' preset effects which run autonomously after one command per bulb.
findings.detail: color-mode 'sequence' triggers built-in animated presets on compatible bulbs/strips (speed not adjustable via API per issue #205). Exploiting on-device effects converts a continuous animation from ~N calls/sec forever into N one-shot calls per scene change — likely the only cloud-path way to get living, breathing canopy motion within quota; bench must confirm which A19 SKU presets exist and how they look.

findings.claim: Ecosystem map beyond jdeath: Emkraan/homeassistant-hubspace (created Jul 27, 2026, pushed Sep 19, 2026, 0 stars) is a from-scratch rival focused on exactly this project's failure modes (per-device availability, self-healing, stale-data tolerance, proactive token refresh) with a patched vendored aioafero; matterbridge-hubspace bridges to Matter (30s/min 5s polls); homebridge-hubspace and a Hubitat port exist; hubspace-ng is dead (last push Mar 2, 2024, v0.0.4); no real Node-RED node or MQTT bridge exists.
findings.detail: Emkraan's patch list is effectively a free failure-mode catalog for the kiosk bridge team (token deadlock, 500/502/conn-error retry gaps, silent stale-poll loop) but the project has zero community validation — mine its diffs, don't adopt it blind. matterbridge-hubspace (Apache-2.0, Node 20.19+, 130 commits, 0 stars) offers a second protocol path (Matter) still backed by the same cloud. For the bespoke replacement-app pitch: the entire community stack is unofficial, ToS-gray, reverse-engineered, and Afero has ignored cooperation requests — a client-facing product on this API carries platform-shutoff risk with Myko as precedent.

research.headline: The Hubspace protocol is fully mapped publicly (Keycloak PKCE auth, semantics2 metadevice REST, Conclave TLS push, encrypted BLE onboarding) and is 100% cloud with no local control path — but no public capture shows whether the app's group/scene apply is one server-side call or N per-device calls; the legacy Afero platform has a one-call server-side rules-execute primitive, and one mitmproxy session of the app controlling a 40-bulb group is the decisive missing experiment.

findings.claim: The community reverse-engineered stack is consolidated in Expl0dingBanana/aioafero (renamed from aiohubspace; predecessor hubspace_async), currently v9.3.0 released 2026-09-15, and it is the engine behind jdeath/Hubspace-Homeassistant; all older projects (hubspace-ng, sajmonr/homebridge-hubspace, jan-leila/hubspace-py, zenion, ctrlcmdshft fork, kirchmeyer/matterbridge-hubspace) document the same API surface.
findings.detail: aioafero exposes typed controllers over 'AferoBridgeV1'; it is actively maintained (releases within the last week as of Sep 19 2026) and now includes a Conclave push client and mitmproxy documentation for capturing the official app. The repo's tests ship a real anonymized account dump (tests/v1/data/raw_hs_data.json) showing metadevice typeIds: metadevice.home, metadevice.room, metadevice.device only.

findings.claim: Auth is Keycloak OAuth2 Authorization Code + PKCE (S256) against accounts.hubspaceconnect.com, realm 'thd', public client_id 'hubspace_android', redirect_uri 'hubspace-app://loginredirect'; endpoints are /auth/realms/thd/protocol/openid-connect/auth, /auth/realms/thd/login-actions/authenticate (HTML form POST of username/password), and /auth/realms/thd/protocol/openid-connect/token; initial scope 'openid offline_access', refresh scope 'openid email offline_access profile'; access tokens are treated as living ~118 seconds so everything runs on refresh tokens.
findings.detail: Verbatim from aioafero src/aioafero/v1/v1_const.py and v1/auth.py: AFERO_CLIENTS['hubspace'] = {API_DATA_HOST: 'semantics2.afero.net', API_HOST: 'api2.afero.net', AUTH_DEFAULT_CLIENT_ID: 'hubspace_android', AUTH_DEFAULT_REDIRECT_URI: 'hubspace-app://loginredirect', AUTH_OPENID_HOST: 'accounts.hubspaceconnect.com', AUTH_REALM: 'thd'}. PKCE verifier = 40 random bytes base64url; DEFAULT_TOKEN_TIMEOUT=118s with 2s expiry buffer. The login flow scrapes the Keycloak login form action URL then exchanges the code; no client secret.

findings.claim: A specific Android-webview User-Agent is used to avoid Afero-side filtering: 'Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 15; ${client_name} Build/test; wv) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Chrome/138.0.7204.63 Mobile Safari/537.36', and requests explicitly set a 'host' header (semantics2.afero.net for state calls, api2.afero.net for platform calls).
findings.detail: The UA template lives in AFERO_GENERICS['DEFAULT_USERAGENT']; controllers/base.py sets headers {'host': API_DATA_HOST, 'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8'} on state PUTs. The library also hardcodes MAX_RETRIES=3 and pauses per-device state polling after 3 consecutive 403s (STATE_FETCH_FORBIDDEN_LIMIT), which is direct evidence Afero serves 403s to clients it dislikes — treat UA and pacing as load-bearing.

findings.claim: Device/API surface: GET https://semantics2.afero.net/v1/accounts/{accountId}/metadevices (optionally ?expansions=state) lists everything; state writes are PUT https://semantics2.afero.net/v1/accounts/{accountId}/metadevices/{deviceId}/state with body {'metadeviceId': id, 'values': [{'functionClass', 'functionInstance', 'value', 'lastUpdateTime'}...]} — multiple attributes per bulb batch into ONE PUT, but each PUT addresses exactly ONE metadevice; account id comes from GET api2.afero.net/v1/users/me.
findings.detail: One PUT can set power+color-mode+RGB+brightness together for one bulb (states list), so a 40-bulb zone change is 40 HTTP PUTs in the community stack, not 160 — but still N calls fanned out from the client. The current Flutter app hits a /v2/ variant (semantics2 '/v2/accounts/<account>/metadevices/<id>/state' per the Sep 2026 native teardown, and both '/v1/accounts/' and '/v2/accounts/' string constants exist in the app binary) while aioafero still successfully uses /v1/. Multi-function devices split into child metadevices with suffixed ids ('-light', '-fan').

findings.claim: CRITICAL QUESTION status — no public capture proves how the official app applies a scene/group; but three hard facts bound the answer: (1) the community write path is strictly N per-device cloud PUTs; (2) the Afero platform has a server-side account rules engine where one Rule holds deviceActions for MANY devices and is executed server-side by a single POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/rules/{ruleId}/actions with body {'type':'execute_actions'}; (3) the current Hubspace Flutter app's SDK (afero_dart_sdk) contains an 'AferoClientSceneMixin' and 'AferoClientFavoritesMixin', proving scenes are first-class API entities in the shipping app, not client-side loops over the metadevice PUT.
findings.detail: The rules primitive is in Afero's own open-source AferoJavaSDK: GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/rules?expansions=schedule, POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/rules (Rule = {deviceActions: [{deviceId, attributes: [{id, value}], durationSeconds}], deviceFilterCriteria, schedule/scheduleId, deviceGroupId, enabled}), and ruleExecuteActions POST returning ActionResponse[]. RuleExecuteBody is literally {'type': 'execute_actions'}. The Rule model even carries a deviceGroupId field. Whether the hubspace_android Keycloak token authorizes these api2.afero.net rules endpoints, and whether the app's Groups feature uses them versus N v2-semantics PUTs, is unverified — no public repo references a Hubspace scenes endpoint ('metadevice.scene' and 'AferoClientSceneMixin' each return zero/one GitHub code hits, the one being the decompile itself). This is bench-test #1.

findings.claim: Realtime state is NOT a websocket: it is 'Conclave', a raw TLS TCP socket speaking newline-delimited JSON with optional zlib compression; the client POSTs api2.afero.net/v1/accounts/{accountId}/conclaveAccess {'user': true, 'softHub': false} to receive {host, port, token, channel_id} (e.g. conclave-stream1.afero.net; official SDK default conclave-stream.afero.io:443), then sends a login frame and receives 'attr_change' and 'status_change' private events plus bare-newline heartbeats.
findings.detail: Both the official AferoJavaSDK (ConclaveClient.java: DEFAULT_HOST 'conclave-stream.afero.io', DEFAULT_PORT 443, login/say/whisper messages, ERROR_CODE_INVALID_TOKEN 906) and aioafero's conclave module (handshake→login→welcome, heartbeat ack, read timeout 75s or 2x server heartbeat, reconnect backoff 1s→60s doubling, REST reconciliation on reconnect) agree. Conclave attr_change events carry raw numeric attribute ids that must be mapped per-device-profile via each metadevice's description.functions[].values[].deviceValues[].key — the semantic (functionClass/functionInstance) and raw-attribute models are two views of the same state. jdeath's HA integration ships Conclave push enabled by default since the 'dev-conclave-support' release, with REST polling demoted to a 900s true-up — this is the kiosk's state-feedback channel.

findings.claim: BLE onboarding was reverse-engineered in depth in September 2026 (go-go-golems/wesen project): bulbs expose GATT service 7a5a0068-6469-7545-4c42-6e6162696b with characteristic pairs 7a5afe01/02 (setup), 7a5afffb/fc (negotiation), 7a5afffd/fe (encrypted messaging), 7a5afe03/04 (ack/credit); the session is ECDH-derived AES-128-GCM (12-byte nonce, truncated 6-byte tag), envelope 'u16le len | u32le seq | ciphertext | tag[6]', inner frame 'u16le length | u8 type | u8 flags | u16le attribute_id | u16le value_length | value'.
findings.detail: The phone acts as an Afero 'softhub' (io.afero.hubby JNI wrapper around native libhubsy.so, Flutter platform channel 'afero.io/softhub_method'): provisioning APIs are getWifiSSIDListFromHub(deviceId) → bulb scans and returns SSID list over the encrypted BLE session, sendWifiCredentialToHub(deviceId, ssid, password), requestSetupModeAction + SecondFactor for secure association, and WIFI_SETUP_STATE_ATTRIBUTE tracks progress — i.e., Wi-Fi credentials go phone→BLE→bulb, but association/authorization round-trips through the cloud. Practical consequence for a 200-bulb install: onboarding requires the app + live internet per bulb, there is no documented offline/batch provisioning, and moving to a new SSID means re-onboarding every bulb (plan install-week Wi-Fi SSID/password to exactly match what bulbs were provisioned with).

findings.claim: There is NO usable local-network or BLE control path post-setup: the Sep 2026 native/BLE investigation concluded 'Internet-independent smart control is not demonstrated' — the phone can relay pre-encrypted payloads over BLE but cannot construct/authorize commands offline, Afero's own docs describe the mobile app as an internet gateway ('hub') for BLE products, and the community consensus (jdeath README: Hubspace is '100% reliant on the cloud', updates slow) matches; hobbyists wanting local control physically replace the Afero radio board with an ESP32 (dresslerc/esphome-afero).
findings.detail: The BLE writeup's status: 59 captured envelopes reconstructed, crypto model validated, but 'The light is not yet independently controlled offline' and session-key extraction remains unsolved — so for the Oct 20-23 install, treat BLE as onboarding-only and plan for hard cloud dependency (the <60s recovery-after-internet-loss acceptance test is entirely about Conclave reconnect + REST re-sync, not any local fallback). Also note Wi-Fi bulbs themselves hold their own cloud connection ('direct' status field in Conclave status_change events distinguishes direct-to-cloud vs via-hub devices). Plan-B Art-Net remains the only sub-second-guaranteed path.

findings.claim: The underlying Afero platform API (api2.afero.net /v1, documented in Afero's own devdocs and legacy SDK) offers a raw per-device write path the semantics layer wraps: POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/devices/{deviceId}/actions {'type':'attribute_write','attrId':N,'data':'<hex little-endian>'} and POST .../devices/{deviceId}/requests with WriteRequest[]; official docs warn these are ASYNCHRONOUS — 'the API call may return before the actual read/write takes place' — so HTTP 2xx is not confirmation a bulb changed; confirmation must come from Conclave attr_change events.
findings.detail: This asynchronous-ack semantics is the single most important fact for the acceptance targets: '95% of scene changes visibly start <2s' must be measured bulb-side (Conclave echo or camera), not by HTTP latency. The devices/{deviceId}/versions endpoint (used by aioafero every 6h) and GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/devices?expansions=state%2Cattributes%2Ctimezone%2Ctags also exist on the platform host.

findings.claim: Platform-risk context: 'Myko' (Ace Hardware), the other Afero-based consumer brand that aioafero used to support, was migrated OFF Afero onto Tuya ('Myko+') between 2025-12-10 and 2026-01-31, breaking all reverse-engineered integrations for those users; aioafero's current constants file now lists only the 'hubspace' client. Hubspace itself remains on Afero as of Sep 2026 and Home Depot keeps investing (Hubspace Connect switch-to-light direct pairing; the House Beautiful Whole Home program), but a partner-initiated backend migration is a demonstrated, not hypothetical, failure mode for cloud-API-dependent installs.
findings.detail: jdeath issues #219 'Myko+ No Longer Supported' and #223 'Myko+ migration' document devices silently disappearing from the integration as accounts migrated. For a 6-week activation window the risk is negligible, but for pitching a bespoke long-lived replacement app to the client afterward, this is the headline dependency risk (no contract, no deprecation policy, endpoints can move from v1 to v2 silently — the app already uses /v2 semantics while the community is on /v1).

findings.claim: A bespoke kiosk/operator app is highly feasible on the documented surface (Keycloak login, metadevices list, per-device state PUT, Conclave push), and aioafero even ships mitmproxy how-to docs (docs/mitm/: install.rst, daily_use.rst — filter hosts accounts.hubspaceconnect.com, api2.afero.net, semantics2.afero.net, package io.afero.partner.hubspace) that make the decisive group/scene capture a documented afternoon task rather than novel research; a recent independent Swift client (Michael-Place/menere HubspaceClient) confirms the auth+transport re-implements cleanly outside Python.
findings.detail: Differentiation for the pitch: official app has no kiosk mode, no multi-account dashboard, no zone choreography; the API supports batched multi-attribute PUTs and push state, enough for a polished guest UX. Risks: ToS (no official public API; the reverse-engineered ecosystem persists openly since 2021 without documented C&D, but a commercial pitch to Home Depot's own client should seek Afero/THD blessing), UA/403 filtering, unpublished rate limits, and silent v1→v2 migration.

bench_tests: DECISIVE: mitmproxy the official Hubspace app (follow aioafero docs/mitm/install.rst + daily_use.rst; package io.afero.partner.hubspace; filter accounts.hubspaceconnect.com, api2.afero.net, semantics2.afero.net) while (a) toggling an app-created Group of 40+ bulbs and (b) creating+applying an app Scene — count HTTP calls: 1 call to a rules/scenes endpoint = server-side fan-out exists and the kiosk should use it; N metadevice PUTs = the app is no better than aioafero and the Python bridge's concurrency IS the architecture.

Rules-engine probe with the kiosk's hubspace_android token: GET https://api2.afero.net/v1/accounts/{accountId}/rules?expansions=schedule (read-only, safe) — if scenes/automations built in the official app appear as Rule objects with deviceActions[], then POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/rules/{ruleId}/actions {"type":"execute_actions"} on a 40-bulb test rule and measure first-to-last bulb spread vs test #3.

Fan-out latency baseline: 40 bulbs on one account, fire 40 parallel PUTs /v1/accounts/{aid}/metadevices/{id}/state via asyncio.gather (each PUT batching power+color+brightness in one values[] list); film at 60fps and measure command-send→first-visible-change (target <2s p95) and first-to-last spread (target <2s); repeat 100x for the zero-wrong-bulb count; also compare /v2/ vs /v1/ state endpoint behavior.

Conclave at scale: open one Conclave session for the 200-bulb canopy account (POST conclaveAccess {'user':true,'softHub':false}); apply scenes continuously for 8h; verify every PUT is echoed as attr_change within budget, log heartbeat gaps, ConclavePushStaleError occurrences, reconnect storms, and whether 200 devices on ONE account even receive complete event coverage (no public data exists at this device count — also confirm account device-count limits by onboarding all 200).

Rate-limit ramp: from one IP/account, ramp semantics2 PUT rate (1→5→10→20→40 req/s) and log first 429/403 and Retry-After headers; separately verify the 3-consecutive-403 state-GET lockout and whether it is per-device, per-account, or per-IP — Home Depot's separate-accounts-per-vignette advice suggests per-account throttling; no public numbers exist.

Token discipline under load: run refresh-token rotation every ~110s for 12h on 5 concurrent accounts (kiosk + 4 iPads) from one venue IP; confirm Keycloak doesn't rotate/invalidate refresh tokens or fingerprint the aioafero UA; capture the exact expires_in Keycloak actually returns.

Recovery drill: kill venue WAN for 5 min mid-show, restore, and time (a) Conclave reconnect (expect 1-60s backoff), (b) REST reconciliation completing, (c) first successful scene apply — validates the <60s recovery target and whether bulbs themselves rejoin cloud fast or need power-cycle.

Provisioning throughput: time BLE onboarding per A19 bulb via the app on the final install SSID (bulbs must be provisioned on the exact SSID/password used at the venue — test that a pre-staged bulb moved to a different SSID requires full re-onboarding), measure failures/retries per 50 bulbs, and test whether 5 phones onboarding in parallel on 5 accounts interfere in a dense 2.4GHz environment.
open_questions: Does the official app send ONE call for a group/scene apply or N per-device calls? (No public capture exists; AferoClientSceneMixin proves a scene API entity, the legacy rules engine proves a one-call primitive, but the wire truth needs the mitm capture.)

What endpoints does AferoClientSceneMixin call — legacy /v1/accounts/{aid}/rules on api2.afero.net, or a newer /v2 semantics scenes resource on semantics2.afero.net — and does the hubspace_android Keycloak token authorize rule create/execute?
Are there per-account device-count or event-throughput ceilings that make 200 bulbs on one account (or one Conclave channel) infeasible, forcing the 5-zone/5-account split?
What are the actual rate limits (req/s, burst, per-IP vs per-account) on semantics2 PUTs and the Keycloak token endpoint?
Is the /v1/ semantics surface on a deprecation path given the app already uses /v2/ (and would a mid-October server change strand the aioafero-based bridge)?
Can a 'user'-type Conclave session WRITE attributes via say/whisper frames (the SDK exposes write primitives historically used by hubs), which would be a lower-latency command path than REST?

Does Afero/THD tolerate or object to a commercial bespoke client (no ToS/API license exists publicly; ecosystem unchallenged since 2021, but the House Beautiful context likely warrants asking Afero directly — Afero is the actual platform vendor behind the partner app)?

Do ~200 always-on RGB A19s on 2.4GHz maintain stable cloud connections through the venue's wired-AP mesh under show-floor RF congestion (the 'direct' Conclave status flag will show per-bulb connectivity)?

research.headline: Every relevant Hubspace device is Leedarson-built ESP32 (FCC-confirmed ESP32-U4WD in the current A19 RGB bulb) speaking an Afero cloud data model that exposes RGB+CCT+named effects and a power-restore setting but NO per-command fade/transition — and the ESP32s ship with download mode eFuse-disabled, so custom firmware on stock bulbs is effectively impossible; plan fades in the bridge or via built-in autonomous effects.

findings.claim: The current EcoSmart A19 RGB Wi-Fi bulb sold at Home Depot is model 12A19060WRGBWH1 (Internet #322660146 single, #329945546 4-pack; Item #1008 588 501), with older 11-series variant 11A19060WRGBWH1 (Internet #318411935) and a clear-filament RGB variant 12CFA1960WRGB01 (Internet #326010996, 2-pack #328233930).
findings.detail: The Use and Care Guide PDF hosted on Home Depot's CDN confirms model, item number, and specs: 120V/60Hz, 8.5W, 800 lumens, 94 lm/W, CRI 90, 5-year (3h/day) warranty, Wi-Fi CERTIFIED + Bluetooth logos, 2.4 GHz network required, and warnings against dimmers and totally enclosed fixtures (thermal constraint relevant to canopy socket density).

findings.claim: The 12A19060WRGBWH1 bulb's FCC ID is 2AB2Q-12A800STQT and the FCC filing explicitly names the SoC: Espressif ESP32-U4WD, with 'other functions disabled via software'; grant date Nov 18, 2022; Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n HT20/HT40 2412-2462 MHz at 0.074W conducted, BLE 1M 2402-2480 MHz at 0.007W.
findings.detail: This is the definitive chip ID for the exact hero-piece bulb: an ESP32 (Xtensa LX6, embedded flash U4-series) running Afero firmware, not Realtek/Beken and not a discrete Afero radio module. Grantee 2AB2Q is LEEDARSON LIGHTING CO., LTD; the manual lists Leedarson America Inc., 300 Technology Court SE Suite 100, Smyrna GA 30082 as FCC responsible party. EcoSmart/Hubspace bulbs are Leedarson ODM products.

findings.claim: Leedarson's universal Hubspace Wi-Fi modules are ESP32-based across generations: LA02301 (FCC 2AB2Q-LA02301, grant 2020) is an 'ESP32-U4WDH SiP with embedded 4MB flash' per its own FCC user manual, and the newer LA02305 (grant 2023, updated through Jan 2026) is again ESP32-U4WDH, Xtensa LX6 up to 160 MHz, Wi-Fi b/g/n to +19 dBm and BLE +8 dBm; an LA02306 module was granted Sep 12, 2025 (chip not yet public).
findings.detail: So 2020-2026 Hubspace lighting/plug/switch hardware is consistently single-family: ESP32 classic with 4MB in-package flash. There is no Beken/Realtek anywhere in the lineup, which rules out OpenBeken/LibreTiny/tuya-cloudcutter-style approaches entirely.

findings.claim: Custom firmware on stock Hubspace devices is effectively blocked: community flashing attempts found the ESP32 bootloader's Download Mode disabled (eFuse-burned), so GPIO0-grounding serial flashing fails; the only proven path is physically replacing the module (documented M5Stack Stamp transplant with LED channels rewired to GPIO25/26/18/19/22).
findings.detail: The Home Assistant thread covers Hubspace-family devices (Defiant HPPA11CWB plug, Commercial Electric recessed kit with Leedarson module LA02301, HPDA311CWB dimmer). A 'Factory' pin enables a 460800-baud serial protocol that remains unreversed. Assume Secure Boot + flash encryption eFuses; treat bulbs (potted, soldered leads, inaccessible serial pads per the EcoSmart disassembly thread) as non-flashable for this project's timeline.

findings.claim: The Afero cloud data model for these bulbs exposes: color-rgb as raw RGB bytes {r,g,b} 0-255 (not hue/sat), color-mode enum (white | color | sequence, plus night-light on some fixtures), numeric color-temperature (A21: 2200-6500K in 100K steps; some fixtures instead expose a discrete named-K list), brightness 1-100%, and named color-sequence effects — and there is NO transition/fade-time parameter anywhere in the light PUT model.
findings.detail: Verified by reading the full aioafero light controller source (set_state signature: on, temperature, brightness, color_mode, color, effect, force_white_mode, numbers, channel — no duration/transition) and the real A21 device dump (tests/v1/data/light-a21-raw.json). Any cross-fade for the Color Canopy must be synthesized by the kiosk bridge as stepped brightness/color writes through the cloud, or delegated to the bulbs' built-in autonomous effects.

findings.claim: Built-in autonomous effects on the A21/A19 family: preset instance = flash, fade-3, fade-7, jump-3, jump-7, custom; custom instance = sleep, july-4th, clarity, focus, wake-up, getting-ready, rainbow, chill, dinner-party, moonlight, valentines-day, christmas, nightlight; plus a speed control (functionClass 'speed'/'color-sequence') ranging -10..+10 step 1.
findings.detail: These run on-bulb with no continuing cloud traffic, which is the cheapest way to get 'living' motion in canopy zones between scene changes. fade-3/fade-7 are slow multi-color cross-fades; jump-3/jump-7 are hard cuts. From the A21 Color CCT Light fixture dump (Ecosmart).

findings.claim: Power-restore behavior is a device setting: functionClass 'restore-values' with enum restored | not-restored | partial-restore (A21 dump shows partial-restore as the active value). This is writable via the same state PUT path as any other function.
findings.detail: For the canopy this means bulbs can be configured to come back in a defined state after a power cut instead of the classic all-bulbs-blast-white — but exact semantics of each option (last state vs default white vs on/off-only restore) need one bench cycle to characterize since no public doc defines them.

findings.claim: BLE stays active after provisioning: every Hubspace device class (bulbs, plugs, locks, transformer) reports both wifi-mac-address AND ble-mac-address states to the cloud; Hubspace officially advertises Bluetooth fallback control from the app when Wi-Fi/internet is down ('pairs via Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, defaults to Wi-Fi, Bluetooth works instead if no connection'); newer fixtures even expose ble-scan-requests/ble-scan-responses functions (bulbs acting as BLE scanners).
findings.detail: Corroborated three ways: aioafero device dumps, Digital Trends/Gearbrain coverage of the BT fallback feature, and an early-stage jdeath/hubspace_ble repo that talks to Defiant locks over BLE and extracts device IDs. BLE fallback is app-only and unreversed for third parties, so the kiosk cannot use it as a control path today — but it is the on-site emergency lever if the venue uplink dies (staff phones in BT range).

findings.claim: Provisioning at scale: each bulb has a unique QR code printed on the housing (and quick start card); QR must be scanned inside the Hubspace app with phone Bluetooth on and in BLE range; scanning a QR for a product on another account TRANSFERS it to the scanning account; manual code entry is the fallback.
findings.detail: Direct from the 12A19060WRGBWH1 Use and Care Guide troubleshooting table. Operationally for 200 bulbs across 5 accounts: keep every quick-start card mapped to its physical grid position, budget ~1min/bulb of app provisioning, and note that account transfer is trivially easy (both a convenience for re-zoning and a risk if the wrong staffer scans a bulb).

findings.claim: A21 bulb SKUs: 100W-equiv color 11A21100WRGBWH1 (Internet #318411937) and 12A21100WRGBWH1 (#322660149, 4-pack #328236200); 100W tunable-white 12A21100WCCT001 (#325841207); NEW 150W-equiv color 13A21150WRGBWH1 (Internet #332600653), whose FCC filing (2AB2Q-13A21150WRGBWH, grant Dec 12 2024) specs 120V 18W, 2550 lumens, 2200-6500K, Wi-Fi+BLE.
findings.detail: If the canopy needs more punch than 800lm A19s, the 13-series A21 at 2550lm is the brightest Hubspace RGB medium-base lamp as of 2025-2026 (3.2x the A19 flux, 18W vs 8.5W — power and heat budget triples). Same Afero data model family.

findings.claim: Defiant Hubspace Wi-Fi deadbolts (retail 2025-2026): Square Satin Nickel HSGC9X2D01AJ (Internet #320280682, $99.88), Aged Bronze HSGC9X7D01AJ (#320546529), Square Compact Matte Black HSGCXX901ALPB (#330353477, $79.97), Satin Nickel HSGC9X2D01AJPB (#327901850), and Fingerprint Aged Bronze HSGCDX7D01APPB (#325761752); cheaper non-Hubspace Defiant biometric models DK02A-MB ($69.88)/KS02A-SN ($52.96) also exist — don't confuse them.
findings.detail: Lock API surface (door-lock dump): lock-control (locked/locking/unlocked/unlocking — cloud-commandable both ways), 10 user PIN slots + admin PIN, keypad-unlock event source, auto-lock with 10-600s delay, battery-level 0-100 step 5, last-event log (app/keypad/voice/manual/auto lock+unlock success/fail), lock-sounds, keypad-lockout, vacation-mode. Locks are Wi-Fi + BLE (both MACs reported).

findings.claim: Hubspace smart plugs: Defiant outdoor 2-outlet HPPA52CWB (Internet #315636835, IP64, two INDEPENDENTLY controllable outlets with physical buttons, 15A/120V) and single-outlet outdoor HPPA51CWB (#316341409); indoor plug HPPA11CWB/HPPA11AWB (#315636834); in-wall smart receptacle Commercial Electric HPKA315CWB (#316692069, $16.88); a Defiant 'Smart Stake Timer' outdoor stake outlet also exists in the Afero device data (class power-outlet).
findings.detail: Plug API is just power on/off + timer (+dark-mode LED setting); no energy monitoring on the indoor plug dump. For the glow-garden fountain, HPPA52CWB's independent duplex outlets are ideal (fountain + string lights on one weatherproof unit). PCWorld reviewed the outdoor plug positively; one HD reviewer notes schedules occasionally stall — use direct commands from the iPad, not schedules.

findings.claim: Hubspace string lights are per-bulb color addressable from the app: Hampton Bay 24-light 48ft RGBW Edison HB-17122-HS black (#320671656) / HB-17122-HS-WT white (#320671655), 12-light 24ft HB-10521-HS (#318145796); 2025 refresh HB-2048SC-WH (#327262854), HB-2048SC-BK (#327262776), HB-1024SC-BK (#327262856) adds 'Party Mode'; HD marketing: 'customize individual bulb colors and create or use preset patterns'.
findings.detail: API confirms individual control: string-light dumps expose functionClass color-individual (instance 'custom', with a '20-segment' hint on the Novolink holiday string fixture) plus color-sequence-v2 with custom-1..custom-4 pattern slots, party-mode toggle, RGBW color-temperature, and effect speed. Granularity is per-segment/per-bulb frames pushed as state writes — fine for static per-bulb scenes, NOT a real-time pixel-streaming protocol.

findings.claim: Pathway/landscape Hubspace line (all RGB+CCT 2700-6500K): Lauderdale 70-lumen 3-tier path light 92899 (Internet #320953182, $39.97), 500-lumen in-ground well light 25252 (#326185912), deck rail light 2-pack 23461 (#326185909), 450-lumen spotlight 3-pack L08557 (#318145795/#326463784), plug-in landscape kit with transformer HB-20P10-BK (#327306033), and the Hampton Bay smart landscape transformer HB-200-1215WIFIB (12V/15V output switch, 3 independently toggleable zones, live watts telemetry, overload-state flag).
findings.detail: The transformer is itself a Hubspace device (class landscape-transformer) — the glow garden can run wired low-voltage path lights on transformer zones for rock-solid switching while color control rides the individual fixtures' own Wi-Fi. PCWorld has also reviewed the Hubspace landscape floodlight line.

findings.claim: There is NO Hubspace humidifier. The Hubspace appliance line covers dehumidifiers (Vissani VAD50PS1AWTS with pump), portable ACs (Home Comfort/GoodHome 12K BTU), thermostats, freezers — but no humidifier exists in Home Depot's Hubspace catalog, and aioafero has a dehumidifier controller only.
findings.detail: Vignette 3's humidifier must be a dumb analog-knob humidifier switched by a Hubspace smart plug (HPPA11CWB indoor), which gives on/off only — no humidity readout in the app. Alternatively pivot the demo to the Vissani dehumidifier or a fan. Plan the script accordingly.

findings.claim: Hubspace ceiling fans: Hampton Bay Zandra 52in (92382 matte black Internet #322700722, 92380 brushed nickel #322700728) — 6-speed reversible DC motor, comfort-breeze preset, dimmable CCT light (6 settings 2700-6500K); Hampton Bay Morland 52in indoor/covered-outdoor (59080 #330756847, 59083 #330756850); Home Decorators Tager 52in N383A-MBK-V8 (#322983364); plus a universal retrofit: Hampton Bay Smart Wi-Fi 4-speed fan remote 76278 (#315169181) for existing AC-motor fans.
findings.detail: API: fan-speed enum fan-speed-6-000/016/033/050/066/083/100, fan-reverse (forward/reverse/in-progress), toggle comfort-breeze, timer, separate light entity with brightness + CCT. Fan and light are cleanly separately addressable — good for a bedroom vignette 'fan on, lights warm' scene.

findings.claim: Fan internals confirm a modular architecture usable for fallback hacks: the Afero/Hubspace ESP32 radio board talks to the fan's motor MCU over plain UART (9600 8N1), polling a status request every ~1 second; two active 2026 projects exploit this — dresslerc/esphome-afero (replace radio board with ESP32 daughterboard, Tager fan documented) and ericyanush/esphome-hubspace-fan (complete working ESPHome component: 6 speeds, direction, light brightness, 6 CCT steps, checksums/keepalive).
findings.detail: This is the ONLY practical custom-firmware path in the ecosystem, and it applies to fans (separable radio module), not bulbs (single-PCB potted). Irrelevant for the 200-bulb canopy but a real plan-C for a single showcase fan if cloud control proves flaky.

findings.claim: The community library is aioafero (renamed from aiohubspace; PyPI aioafero, repo Expl0dingBanana/aioafero, actively pushed as of Sep 19 2026) and the HA integration jdeath/Hubspace-Homeassistant (381 stars) now defaults to 'Conclave' push events for near-real-time state with REST polling demoted to a 15-minute true-up; aioafero ships conclave_client/conclave_protocol modules.
findings.detail: Hardware-side implication: device state changes propagate to the cloud fast enough that Afero runs a push channel — the kiosk bridge should consume Conclave events for confirmation of scene application rather than polling metadevice state. Cloud constants in aioafero: api2.afero.net, semantics2.afero.net (data), accounts.hubspaceconnect.com realm 'thd', client_id 'hubspace_android'.

findings.claim: Hubspace 2.0 app/platform launched Dec 16, 2025 with Circadian Lighting, Warm Dimming, Logarithmic Brightness, 'Hubspace Connect' (binding switches to lights across rooms without wiring), and Vacation Mode — matching new 2025+ device functionClasses seen in dumps: warm-dimming, vacation-mode-enable/group, schedule-pause, micro-hub-soul-mates.
findings.detail: Newer fixtures (Penrose vanity light, recessed-with-trim, RGBCW strips) carry these extra functions; the 12/13-series bulbs bought new in Oct 2026 may present more functions than older teardown-era units. Multi-zone fixtures also introduce per-instance color (brightness/color-mode/color-rgb with 'main'/'trim' instances) and dual-channel RGB+white with a 'mixed' color-mode.

findings.claim: Radio constraints for the 200-bulb canopy: bulbs are 2.4 GHz-only 802.11 b/g/n (channels 1-11, HT20/HT40), ~+18.7 dBm max conducted, WPA2; setup requires phone BLE; Wi-Fi CERTIFIED. The bulb reports wifi-rssi, wifi-ssid, wifi-steady-state and ble-mac to the cloud, so per-bulb RSSI is remotely auditable through the API during install.
findings.detail: Use the wifi-rssi state as a free site-survey tool: after hanging the canopy, pull all 200 RSSI values via aioafero and rebalance APs before tour days. HT40 on 2.4GHz should be disabled AP-side to keep 3 non-overlapping channels for 5 zones x 40 bulbs.

findings.claim: Older 11-series bulb kits used BLE remotes: FCC 2AB2Q-11A19060WRGBK (grant Oct 2021) is the bulb with BLE-remote pairing (0.012W BLE) and 2AB2Q-11A19060WRGBR/R2 are the paired remote controllers — irrelevant to control architecture but explains odd 'R' SKUs in Home Depot listings.
findings.detail: Filament/decorative platform FCC 2AB2Q-A800SG-G1Z (grant Jun 2023) covers 12CFA1960WCCT0x tunable-white filament A19 plus ST19/G25 variants (7W/800lm, 2700-6500K, Wi-Fi+BLE). The MR16 RGB 12MR161050RGB01 (#326011001) exists for accent use.

findings.claim: Known real-world weak points from the HA community: Hubspace devices are 100%-cloud for third-party control ('due to the cloud-first nature... internet connection needs to be available, along with the Hubspace servers'), app/cloud state updates can lag, and one HD reviewer reports plug schedules stalling — no public quantitative latency benchmarks exist for multi-bulb scene fan-out, which is exactly what the Sep 23 bench gate must produce.
findings.detail: Nobody in the community has published 40-bulb-simultaneous-command timing. The aioafero architecture (per-metadevice state PUTs; Conclave for push-back) implies the bridge will issue up to 40 discrete PUTs per zone scene unless semantics2 exposes a group construct — cloud-team research question.

bench_tests: Fade smoothing characterization: command an abrupt color change (e.g., red->blue) and brightness change (100->10%) on one 12A19060WRGBWH1 and film at 240fps; measure whether firmware applies internal ramping (ms of smoothing) or hard-cuts — the API has no transition parameter, so perceived scene-change quality depends entirely on this.

restore-values semantics: for each of restored / not-restored / partial-restore, set a saturated color scene, kill mains power 10s, restore, and record exact power-on state (on/off, color, brightness) and time-to-light; confirms canopy behavior after a breaker trip mid-show and whether bulbs storm the Wi-Fi/cloud on reconnect.

Zone fan-out latency (the go/no-go metric): from the Python bridge via aioafero, PUT a full scene to 40 bulbs on one account/AP; measure Apply->first bulb visibly changing, first-to-last spread, and p95 over 100 scene changes; repeat with all 5 zones (200 bulbs, 5 accounts) firing within 1s of each other to detect cloud rate limiting (watch for HTTP 429/403 from api2.afero.net).

Built-in effect evaluation: run fade-3, fade-7, jump-3, jump-7 and the 13 custom presets (rainbow, christmas, etc.) at speed -10, 0, +10 on a 3x3 bulb grid; assess visual sync drift between adjacent bulbs over 10 minutes (effects free-run per-bulb; if drift is objectionable, canopy 'motion' scenes must be bridge-driven).

Provisioning throughput: time QR-scan onboarding of 10 bulbs to one account (target data: min/bulb), then scan 2 of them from a second account to verify ownership transfer behavior and any de-provisioning lag; extrapolate the 200-bulb install window for Oct 20-23.

Wi-Fi association scaling: join 40 bulbs to a single 2.4GHz AP (HT20, WPA2), confirm all hold association for 8h idle + hourly scene changes with zero drops (bulb wifi-rssi and wifi-steady-state polled via API as the log); repeat at 60 clients to find the practical per-AP ceiling before the 5-AP layout is finalized.

Thermal soak in canopy fixture: mount 9 bulbs at final grid pitch in the actual socket/shroud hardware (manual forbids totally enclosed fixtures), run 8h at 100% white; log external bulb-neck temperature and check for thermal dimming/color shift or dropouts.

BLE fallback drill: disconnect venue WAN, verify Hubspace app on an on-site phone still controls a canopy zone bulb and the Defiant lock over Bluetooth (range test through the vignette wall), and measure recovery time for cloud control after WAN restore (<60s target).

String light custom frames: push per-bulb color-individual frames to HB-17122-HS via the app and (if exposed) via aioafero state PUTs; measure frame apply latency and max sustainable frame rate to decide whether glow-garden 'twinkle' is app-preset-only or bridge-driveable.
Lock demo latency: 50 lock/unlock cycles from an iPad via cloud; record command->motor-start latency distribution and any lockouts; verify last-event state reflects each action for the staff script.
